correctness.rationale: The absolute-value comparison reduces the numerical radius to the upper spectral edge of the positive selfadjoint block Jacobi matrix. Schur complement and the exact half-line resolvent yield the matrix threshold and the unique supercritical root. Strict resolvent monotonicity proves uniqueness; recurrence excludes threshold eigenvectors. For E_ij the rank-one singular norm, hyperbolic secular equation and quadratic expansion are exact. For the two-way two-site example, a 2x2 Loewner principal-minor test gives the quartic. Reconstructed key quantifiers and all boundary cases. A deterministic checker passed 151 supplemental finite comparisons; the universal statement is proved analytically.

originality.rationale: The full-text 2023 extremality paper provides finite-dimensional sufficient tests for symmetric nonnegative T, but not the equivalence and sharp supercritical spectral root for arbitrary nonsymmetric nonnegative finite-support T. The 2020/2021 earlier source gives diagonal results; the Jiang-Spitkovsky paper focuses on the infinite-support scalar T. Those are substantively compared, not treated as novelty proof by title. The threshold recovers prior one-site/diagonal examples, which are credited; originality is assessed only for the general iff finite-matrix formula plus explicit nonsymmetric joint boundary and off-diagonal root/onset.
residual_risks: An older nonindexed finite-rank Birman-Schwinger formula may implicitly subsume the result; finite Green inverses are classical.
The 2021 primary source was read in its publicly accessible full-text HTML representation, rather than an independently obtained typeset PDF; unrelated later sections were not re-reviewed.
No claim is made to independent or exhaustive historical certification.

value.rationale: This solves the lower numerical-radius boundary for every finite nonnegative coupling matrix, including nonsymmetric off-diagonal patterns previously outside the cited sufficient symmetric test. The finite positive Green covariance is explicit for every size, so the result replaces an infinite-operator threshold problem with a sharp computable condition; the unique supercritical secular equation gives the entire numerical-radius curve. The exact two-way coupling quartic demonstrates a genuine interaction boundary, while matrix-unit couplings have a precise depth-dependent critical constant and quadratic onset. These motivated classifications are not merely recomputation of the prior diagonal one-site bound. Sign-changing and infinite support are transparently excluded.
